clue.text: County team’s disadvantage

blocks.note: County Down is in Northern Ireland
a side is a team in a match

explanation.surface: A sports writer bemoans the weak spot of a county club's line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A downside is the drawback or negative aspect of something, the same as a disadvantage.

clue.text: Tool in stream of liquid not beginning to rust

indicators.note: 'not' tells us to leave a letter out of the stream word
the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is taken

blocks.note: a dribble is a thin trickle of liquid
opening letter of rust

explanation.surface: A garden implement left out in the wet must be kept free of rust.
explanation.walkthrough: DRIBBLE loses its R to give DIBBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dibble is a pointed gardener's hand implement used to make holes in soil for planting seedlings.

clue.text: Worried person is said to have this finish

definitions.text: Worried person is said to have this

blocks.clueFragment: Worried person is said to have this
blocks.note: first meaning: a frightened person is said to have 'the ...'
second meaning: to bring something to a close

explanation.walkthrough: To 'have the wind up' is British slang for being scared, so the first part is a whole idiom pointing at the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind up a meeting or business is to conclude it, so the phrasal verb matches finish.

clue.text: Fish are stout swimming around

indicators.note: letters swimming around are moving about freely and so end up in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler notes that some plump fish are swimming about in the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea trout is a migratory brown trout species that spends time in salt water, an example of a fish.

clue.text: Welshman’s platform

blocks.note: Dai is a typically Welsh first name, a crossword stock Welshman
the possessive ending kept as written

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single Welsh person's stage; the possessive is simply DAI'S.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised stage at one end of a hall for speakers or dignitaries.

clue.text: Catholic services getting lots

blocks.note: first meaning: celebrations of the Eucharist in the Catholic Church
second meaning: large quantities

explanation.surface: Catholic church services are drawing big congregations.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun means both Eucharist rites and, informally, great quantities of anything.

clue.text: Affirm, using Bible with an expression suggesting pain

blocks.note: AV is the Authorised Version, the King James Bible
the cry someone gives when hurt

explanation.surface: A witness swears on the Bible while wincing in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To avouch is an old verb meaning to declare or guarantee something as true.

clue.text: Description of key scheme reduced to essentials

definitions.note: describes a kind of key rather than naming one

blocks.note: first meaning: a master key that opens many locks has this name
second meaning: a bare outline or framework of a plan

explanation.surface: A planner explains the key idea of a scheme stripped down to its basics.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton key opens many locks, and a skeleton plan is the minimal framework of something.

clue.text: Supporters making tracks with eleven players finally inside

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of each of the two words before it
inside says the selected letters sit within the tracks word

blocks.note: spoor is the trail of a wild animal
last letters of eleven and players

explanation.surface: Fans follow a football team's progress, eleven players on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eleven players' looks like a side to be turned into XI or TEAM, but 'finally' takes the end of each word. SPO + NS + ORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sponsors are backers who give financial support to a team, event or cause.

clue.text: Favourite child in difficult situation in African country

indicators.note: in places the trouble word within the country name

blocks.note: a West African state
being in a jam means being in trouble

explanation.surface: A beloved son finds himself in trouble while in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: BEN(JAM)IN.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Jacob's youngest son was his most cherished, so the name is used for a parent's best-loved youngest child.

clue.text: Arrive at total

blocks.note: first meaning: to reach a place or decision
second meaning: to add up to a sum, as a bill does

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as reaching a final figure, but the two phrases are separate meanings of one phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means reaching somewhere, and also amounting to a figure when sums are added.

clue.text: Woman, no longer one looking after paper that’s taken over

blocks.note: a woman's name
an ex is a former partner, someone no longer in that role
ED is short for editor, who runs a newspaper

explanation.surface: A woman who has quit editing a newspaper sees it acquired by a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Territory that has been annexed has been seized and incorporated by another state or body.

clue.text: Various bits of velour in art gallery

indicators.note: taking bits of something in various ways breaks it up and puts it back in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Scraps of plush fabric are on display in a museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Louvre in Paris is one of the world's best-known museums of paintings and sculpture.

clue.text: Those who criticise devices to attract attention of residents

definitions.text: devices to attract attention of residents

blocks.note: first meaning: people who disparage or run things down

blocks.clueFragment: devices to attract attention of residents
blocks.note: second meaning: hinged metal fittings on front doors used by callers

explanation.surface: Critics are compared with the fittings visitors bang on a front door.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocking means harsh criticism, and door fittings that callers rap are named the same way.

clue.text: Imagine member of ancient tribe on Yorkshire river

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so the tribesman comes first

blocks.note: the Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Think of an ancient tribesman standing by a river in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form a mental image of it, just as when you envisage it.

clue.text: Shook as one shown the way ahead

blocks.note: qua is Latin-derived for 'in the capacity of', i.e. as
the Roman numeral for one
guided forward

explanation.surface: Someone trembles while being guided along the path in front.
explanation.walkthrough: QUA + I + LED.
explanation.definitionFit: To quail is to flinch or tremble with fear, so quailed matches the past tense shook.

clue.text: North African place of desolation?

blocks.note: first meaning: a Muslim inhabitant of north-west Africa
second meaning: a bleak open upland

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that open heathland is only loosely 'desolate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the name was given to Berber and Arab peoples of the Maghreb, and the same word means bleak upland heath.

clue.text: Valve head of plumbing company installed in store

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
things installed in somewhere are fitted inside it

blocks.note: stock is goods held in store
first letter of plumbing
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: The boss of a plumbing firm fits a valve in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: STO(P CO)CK.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopcock is a tap on a water pipe used to turn the supply on or off.

clue.text: Horse with energy carrying everyone over street?

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside another
in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it in the entry

blocks.note: go means drive or energy
all means everybody
way appears in street names

explanation.surface: A lively horse carries everybody across the road.
explanation.walkthrough: G(ALL)O above WAY. The question mark admits that a horse carrying everyone is fanciful.
explanation.definitionFit: The Galloway is a small sturdy breed of pony from south-west Scotland.

clue.text: Beginning to stand trial for activity on farm

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter only

blocks.note: opening letter of stand
a hearing is a court trial

explanation.surface: A farmer is about to go on trial over something done on the farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearing is removing the wool from sheep, a seasonal job on a sheep farm.

clue.text: Contemptible person? Just a bit, hiding love

indicators.note: something hiding another keeps it out of sight inside itself

blocks.note: a tad is a small amount
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone shows only a little affection, keeping their love concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: T(O)AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a toad is a figurative insult for a loathsome, repulsive individual.

clue.text: The curt drunk in foreign city

indicators.note: a drunk lurches about, so the words stagger into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rude drunk on holiday in a city abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Utrecht is a historic university city in the central Netherlands, so it is a city outside Britain.

clue.text: Cleaner gets only half what customer pays

indicators.note: only half means the second half of the word is dropped

blocks.note: a char is a British word for a cleaning woman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady complains she receives only half of what clients pay.
explanation.walkthrough: GETS keeps its front half, GE.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is the price or fee asked for goods or a service.

clue.text: Occupant dealt with by letter

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who lives in a property
second meaning: a 'letter' here is one who lets property, a landlord

explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like correspondence, but read it as one who lets out property: such a person deals with renters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant is a person renting and living in a house or flat from its owner.

clue.text: Have another look at what could turn out to be dearer

indicators.text: what could turn out to be
indicators.note: what something could turn out to be is a different form of it, so the letters change order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopper checks again something that might prove more expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: To reread a text is to go through it a second time, giving it a fresh look.

clue.text: Fish and chips mostly cooked with lard

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter
food that is cooked is transformed, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe for fish and chips fried in lard.
explanation.walkthrough: CHIPS loses its S; the remaining letters join LARD in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: The pilchard is a small oily sea fish of the herring family, often sold canned.

clue.text: Composer to give a verse new setting

indicators.note: giving words a new setting rearranges them into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A songwriter sets a poem to fresh music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting' sounds musical, as composers set verse, but here it signals the reordering.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgard Varèse was a French-born American modernist who wrote experimental orchestral and electronic music.

clue.text: Upset produced by iron-bound extremist characters

indicators.note: something bound is wrapped round, so the iron symbol encloses the other letters

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
the extreme letters of the alphabet, first and last

explanation.surface: Someone is disturbed by fanatics bound in iron chains.
explanation.walkthrough: F(AZ)E.
explanation.definitionFit: To faze someone is to disconcert or fluster them, an informal synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Pull number back getting ahead

indicators.note: going back means reading the words from end to start

blocks.note: to draw is to pull
the usual abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: An oarsman pulls back and the boat moves forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Onward is an adverb meaning forward in space or time, so it fits ahead.

clue.text: Assign numbers to a drink to be stored by head

indicators.note: something stored by another is kept inside it

blocks.note: pate is an old word for the top of the head
taken as written
a spirit

explanation.surface: Somebody tots up a numbered drink they will hold in their head.
explanation.walkthrough: The drink is not added at either end: the head word opens after its first letter to take it in. Pate is an old, now jokey word for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To paginate a document is to give each page a number in sequence.

clue.text: ‘Essential to get eastern money back’ (economist)

indicators.note: back means the money word is read from right to left

blocks.note: key means crucial
the sen is a small coin of Japan and other East Asian countries

explanation.surface: A quoted maxim about recovering money from the East, attributed to an economist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastern' looks like the usual E, but it belongs with 'money' to describe an Asian coin.
explanation.definitionFit: John Maynard Keynes was the influential British economist behind Keynesian theory.

clue.text: Reportedly hung around to be given a handicap

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: hung around means stayed waiting

explanation.surface: A racehorse loitering at the start is penalised.
explanation.walkthrough: In handicap horse races stronger horses carry extra weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A weighted competitor carries extra load or a disadvantage to even out the contest.
